findings.title: Harness/provider infrastructure termination becomes ordinary no-final in canonical completion and suite accounting
findings.evidence: The bridge stops immediately on a provider transport/HTTP failure or a check feedback kind of infrastructure-error, then closes the unchanged workspace. With no submit event, workspace.close computes no-final-submission even when the bridge, rather than the model, removed the opportunity to submit. trajectory.final_outcome copies that value. Existing suite accounting consumes the same child completion, so stop text alone does not make the target a distinct unscored infrastructure outcome.

findings.impact: Selection is correctly retained, but causal outcome classification is not preserved in the canonical completion/rollup. A later consumer using those records can count provider/runtime failures as model missing finals instead of keeping them unscored. model_measurement=false prevents an authorized score claim; it does not repair this record contract.
findings.required_resolution: Design a separately reviewed canonical external-termination mechanism or equivalent accounting boundary that retains every selected target and records unscored provider/verifier infrastructure distinctly. It must never override a genuine reserved final or its result. Define protocol-error, actual no-final and interrupted cases explicitly, test the suite rollup, and preserve partial evidence. Do not silently reinterpret or patch the already accepted workspace/runtime in this packet.

findings.title: Returned provider/model identity is recorded opportunistically but not bound to the frozen declaration
findings.evidence: Preflight compares provenance.model to the requested model, but never checks provenance.model_version against the returned model identity. function_call requires a response ID but permits missing/nonmatching response.model; seen_calls tracks function-call IDs, not response IDs. Identity/usage fields are only copied into the step record after tool execution succeeds.

findings.impact: A compiler verdict can be retained as valid independently of model identity, but these records are not yet admissible as an identified provider/model trajectory. A declared snapshot/version can disagree with or be absent from the returned identity without a typed identity failure. The fake verifier's accepted status in these probes is not a real Lean acceptance or an actual provider anomaly.
findings.required_resolution: Specify and enforce the requested-ID/returned-model/version relation, including any explicit alias-resolution policy; require meaningful returned identity, detect repeated response IDs, and preserve identity/usage before tool dispatch where available. Identity failure must be a distinct non-admissible trajectory cause without replacing an already genuine compiler final. Keep provenance_authenticated=false; HTTPS and raw IDs are not cryptographic provider attestation.

positive_checks: Initial model content is assembled from exactly the canonical prompt.json and Solution.lean.txt, checked against the current canonical task descriptor. It does not glob the operator directory or directly append oracle/reference/challenge/configuration contents. The unit nongold/path-sentinel checks passed.

The only declared custom tool is lean_workspace with strict action/source schema, both properties required and additionalProperties=false. The request disables parallel tool calls, forces the one named function and enables no hosted retrieval/shell/code-execution tool. Unknown/multiple/duplicate-key/incomplete calls fail without running their supplied Lean.

The normal stateless loop preserves all returned reasoning/message/function-call items, including opaque encrypted reasoning, and appends the actual matching function_call_output ID. Its include value is accepted as compatible guidance in the official reasoning documentation. This is a static/API-contract check, not a successful live round trip.

The model's source remains data passed to the accepted workspace; no host Lean/shell fallback is introduced. Oversized final source is reserved by workspace.act, becomes invalid-submission and remains selected rather than being executed or replaced.

Fresh transcript paths, exclusive bridge locking, model-session.json reservation before the first HTTP call, zero automatic retries and partial started/finished records limit silent replay. A KeyboardInterrupt probe in the existing unit suite preserves the reservation; ordinary action locking/first-final enforcement remain in the accepted workspace.

API call count and output-token/body bounds are frozen before collection. The documentation correctly states that these are not a dollar-cost ceiling and that input/reasoning or interrupted requests may be billed; spending authorization is not implied.

The CLI removes OPENAI_API_KEY from child-process environment before workspace execution. The standard transport uses a fixed HTTPS endpoint, suppresses redirects and checks direct raw-body credential echo before archiving. Unit tests use only a dummy key and mocked opener; no real credential handling was exercised.

All bridge trajectories keep model_measurement=false and provenance_authenticated=false. Controlled fixture transport is explicitly labeled, and no test result is promoted into native08/model acceptance or new mathematical credit.
boundary_notes_not_additional_acceptance: MODEL.md's non-exposure language should distinguish direct initial provider inputs from compiler-mediated feedback. The accepted sandbox intentionally permits readonly access to public mounted task/runtime/dependency files. Submitted Lean can attempt to print readable container data into bounded diagnostics. The bridge does not itself append challenge/configuration/oracle material, and the container has no oracle mount, but there is no new guarantee that challenge/configuration/public dependency content cannot appear through feedback. provided-prompt-template-only is not enforced closed-book isolation, as the docs otherwise acknowledge.

Transcript hashes are operator evidence under the trusted/quiescent operator assumption, not immutability against a malicious writer. The bridge has no independent sealed-trajectory validation command in this packet. Partial interrupted collection must remain inspectable rather than being counted as a successful sealed run.
The urllib timeout is a transport timeout, not demonstrated here as a whole-call absolute deadline against every slow-response pattern. No broader provider timeout/security claim was validated.
